one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing and embarrassing.

I reported a member’s public post containing statements about kicking, throwing and physically fighting dogs, including a specific reference to a dog by name and a statement that the dog should “count her days.”

Instead of simply allowing the evidence to be reviewed objectively, the response was to defend the member.

That’s especially embarrassing considering the Nation itself declared a State of Emergency over dog attacks and public safety and told members to report these concerns.

If a dog is dangerous, investigate it. If a person’s statements are concerning, investigate those too. The rules should not change depending on who is involved.

You cannot tell people to use the proper reporting system and then undermine that system by immediately defending one of your own members.

Accountability needs to apply to everyone—not just people the Nation finds convenient to hold accountable.

1/5.

Living in the same conditions as the others with no AC/ no hot water/ poor ventilation with high humidity levels and fire alarms back to back.
If you’re considering coming here… DON’T!!!
2300$/month btw…

Wrote a review 1 month ago
Since my last review.......more false fire alarms, multiple days without hot water nor A/C, mushrooms in lockers due to insufisant ventilation(which i brought up multiple months ago) and another change of management.......
No update from property management on everything that's not working or on the false fire alarm.....no answer to tenants e-mail requesting details and asking to have the services they are paying for.
This building is the closest you will ever get from the worst experience of your life(except if your enjoying sleeping in a 85% humidity environment, not being able to take a shower or give your childs a bath for multiple days in a row and love the life without A/C lifestyle).

Can't wait to see the AI answer to my review telling me they know and they are taking care of everything i'm writing......which is in reality 100% BS

one_star_reviews.text:
(Update on Oct 12th)

I opened my window to air out the room and the screen fell off on its own. So much for the "high-end finish" some reviews mention. This is also a big safety concern. For those who have pets/kids, please be aware and pay attention to your windows!

(Updates as of October 9th)

Moved in on July 1st. More than three months later, these issues are still unresolved:

- Found out my balcony work was never completed. I contacted the administration two weeks ago but still haven’t received an update.

- Still no bathroom towel bar or toilet paper holder.

- Still living with a bulky, noisy portable AC unit with no central ac/ventilation running.

- Parking lot still has NO lighting, yet we’ve experienced four power outages over the past few weeks due to electrical work.

- Still no Canada Post deliveries, you have to go pick them up yourself. I do get other packages delivered from Amazon.

(Original review)
Yes, they make you sign the lease acknowledging new construction delays. I understood that going in. What I didn't expect was the scale of "not ready." There's a difference between some delays and what's actually happening here:

- No AC in July. Apparently, the building's AC system is a specialized eco-friendly unit imported from another country, and it's currently stuck at customs. One has to wonder: when exactly was this ordered? Portable AC units have been distributed since as an interim solution, but it's bulky and loud.

- No mail delivery. Canada Post refuses to deliver because of ongoing construction and the address not being routed correctly. And it's not just them, most of my Amazon orders don't make it either. You're essentially invisible. Every package is either returned or has to be picked up manually at a nearby location.

- The parking lot is basically a haunted house. Completely dark, motion-sensored only. You walk in and there's nothing until you trigger the lights yourself. It is actually a lot brighter in the photo.

- The ground floor isn't complete, in a 7-story building. Entire corridors feel like a ghost town, with units still visibly under active construction. So, the air quality is really bad.

- The elevator went out of service within 2 days of move-in, for over 6 hours, with no communication to tenants until much later. Stairs it was. It was out of service again today, and my sofa delivery couldn't be completed and was left at the lobby.

- Basic fixtures missing at move-in: bathroom mirror, towel holder, toilet paper holder. Everything feels rushed, and it shows in the finishes.

- There was no hot water for the first week. Now it takes 10–15 minutes to come through every morning. It's a daily inconvenience that shouldn't exist in new construction.

- The kitchen sink water pressure gets weaker by the day. likely due to construction debris and materials clogging the pipes. See photo. I've been manually unclogging it myself.

And while Phase 1 is in this state, Phase 2 is already being advertised for leasing... why?

To anyone who already signed, I'm sorry, we're in this together. To anyone who hasn't: the promotional rate is tempting, but unless you're planning to move in by November, and I genuinely hope the building is fully done by then, I wouldn't recommend it.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with Kevin Caspersz and this firm started with a good working relationship. Unfortunately, as the circumstances of my case changed, I felt the strategy failed to adapt, and over time I was left feeling that the focus shifted far more toward billing and money than toward my needs as a client.

I experienced repeated requests for additional retainers, sometimes on short notice, even when I understood my account to be current and funds remained on account. At times, I was left with the understanding that work on my matter would not continue until additional funds were provided. What began as a relationship in which I had confidence ultimately ended in a significant dispute over fees and billing.

I am not commenting on Kevin's abilities as a lawyer, but specifically on my experience as his client. I was extremely disappointed with how the relationship ended and, based on my personal experience, I would not recommend Kevin Caspersz or this firm.

UPDATE SEPTEMBER 30, 2026, FOLLOWING THE FIRM'S RESPONSE:

I fully understood the requirement to maintain funds in trust and complied with requests to replenish my retainer. That was never the issue raised in my review. My concern was the manner, timing and frequency of those requests and, more broadly, the treatment I experienced as a client, particularly with respect to billing and payment requests and the way our relationship was ultimately ended.

UPDATE: The response from the store is NOT an accurate representation of what happened.

Nobody warned me beforehand that I was not allowed to hold the hair bun near my hair to check the colour. The staff member only approached me after I did so and told me that because I had touched it with my hair, I HAD to buy it. I explained that the colour didn’t match and that I didn’t want it, but she refused to accept that.

I even asked where this policy was posted or communicated, but I was not shown any notice. Instead, I was given a comparison to a toothbrush, which I did not find reasonable since the bun was not sealed.

This was Never about the money. I was already purchasing other items from the store. I simply did not want to buy a bun that didn’t match my hair.

What made the experience even worse was the way the staff member discussed the situation with another employee while making expressions in front of me, which I found extremely humiliating and disrespectful. I was then told NOT to come back to the store.

If I had been clearly informed of a policy beforehand, I would have respected it. The problem was the way I was treated and the fact that the store’s response now describes the situation differently from what actually happened.

This is why I stand by my review. The customer service was extremely disappointing and, in my experience, the worst I have encountered.

Worst Experience Ever😡i wish i can give 0 star..

I visited BSW Beauty today and unfortunately had a very unpleasant experience with one of the customer service staff.

I was looking at a hair bun and simply held it near my hair to check whether the colour matched. The staff member came over and told me that because I had touched it with my hair, I was now required to purchase it. I explained that the colour did not match my hair and that I did not want to buy it.

I asked where it was stated that customers were not allowed to check the product against their hair, especially since the bun was not sealed or packaged. She compared it to a toothbrush, saying that you cannot try a toothbrush before buying it. However, I don't think that comparison makes sense because toothbrushes are sealed for hygiene reasons, whereas this hair bun was not.

I was happy to purchase other items from the store, but I refused to purchase the bun simply because I didn't need it and the colour didn't match. Instead of handling the situation professionally, I was told not to come back to the store.

I have never experienced customer service like this. If there is a policy that customers cannot put the product near their hair to check the colour, it should be clearly communicated before customers handle the item.

Very disappointing and disrespectful experience. I will definitely not be returning.

one_star_reviews.text: Despite appreciating the existence of a bilingual publishing house in Ottawa, I had a very bad experience after purchasing a book online for a university course. I placed my order on September 10th and, aside from the email I received with my order confirmation, I had no further communication. I waited a week, then tried calling their phone number. I was directed to voicemail where I left my name, phone number, and order number with a brief description requesting an order update. I never received a call back, so a week later I called again and was once more redirected to voicemail. I left the same information, but since it was now September 21st and university classes had resumed on September 9th, I was falling further and further behind. I found their email address and finally received a reply informing me that my order was being prepared and shipped. Furthermore, I was supposed to receive it within a week. Again, a week later, I still hadn't received anything in the mail, so on September 29th, I sent a second email requesting an update, which never received a reply. Since I needed the book for my university course, I went to the store to see if I could pick it up in person. So, yesterday, I traveled from my suburb to the city center to collect my book, which was supposed to be delivered. The employee who was there was very helpful and kind, and I'm very grateful that she was able to give me the book, but I could see that she didn't have access to the system and therefore couldn't give me an update on my order or whether it had actually been completed. Honestly, I hope I never have to deal with this publishing house again, given the lack of communication and the significant delays they caused me in my university course.

one_star_reviews.text:
Sadly, I no longer recommend this church.

I used to genuinely enjoy this church and was heavily involved, volunteering twice a week plus special events and holidays. I felt valued and treated well—until I said I needed to step back.

After more than two years of regularly volunteering, I explained that I am in a season of grief and simply need time to rest, so I would not be committing to weekly volunteering for the upcoming season. Rather than having that decision respected, I was immediately told, “Nope. I don’t accept that.”

I explained that I was not asking anyone to agree with my decision; I was simply asking that it be respected. Instead, I was told that my decision was “unbiblical” and “unwise.” When I reiterated that I needed to step away from life group as well, I was told that I was an adult and therefore they had to respect my decision to step away from life group—“just like if you decide to leave the church, leave the community, leave your faith and denounce Christ.” I had said none of those things. I had simply said I needed to step back.

I was also told that not participating in a weekly two-hour life group was essentially like “deciding not to drink water,” and that life group should be my #1 priority, even ahead of work. When I explained that I work two jobs to support myself and pay my bills, I was told that putting work before life group meant I was “putting money before God” and that money was a “stronghold” in my life.

What was particularly concerning to me was that when I disagreed with leadership, the conversation did not feel like an opportunity for genuine dialogue. It felt like an attempt to convince me that my boundary was wrong until I changed my mind. I was also told that I could speak with another leader, while simultaneously being told that the pastoral staff all agreed with the same position.

I am sharing this review because I wish I had known what to expect before becoming involved.

If you are looking for a church where leadership will respond to a personal boundary with understanding and compassion—even when they disagree with your decision—I unfortunately cannot say that was my experience here.

I encourage anyone considering this church to read the attached screenshots and make their own judgment about the interactions for themselves.

Very disappointing experience. We only stopped here because we arrived late at our campsite at Fairmont Resort and both restaurants there were already closed.

The atmosphere was cramped with a strange seating arrangement, but we didn’t want to judge a book by its cover and still had high hopes. Unfortunately, the food did not feel “farm to kitchen” at all. The market was mostly packaged branded noodles, coffee, hot sauces and other miscellaneous products rather than fresh or homemade items.

I ordered the pear and goat cheese salad with chicken and stopped eating after one bite because the chicken tasted off. My husband ordered the ribs, which tasted previously frozen/prepared, and the heavily seasoned fries didn’t taste homemade either. The homemade lemonade tasted mostly like water with a splash of lemon.

Our bill was around $80 and we barely touched our meals. The young man serving us was very kind, but the older waitress came across quite abrupt and aggressive. Overall, the experience and quality did not match the “Farm Kitchen Market” name or our expectations.

So, I wasted my time and money going to this workshop! Additionally, to make up for my disappointment and dissatisfaction of them not having the specific pieces that I wanted to use that they had posted on their website, they offered to custom order my pieces so I could come back and make the necklace and bracelet that I specifically wanted to make, which I agreed to do. They said it would take approximately 1 month to receive the items and that they would contact me once they received them so I could return to make the specific bracelet and necklace that I had planned to make, which I agreed to do. However, after they confirmed and we agreed that they were going to order those specific pieces for me (photos attached) they instead contacted me 2 days after the workshop to inform me that they were just going to issue me a refund instead since they said they do not typically accommodate any special orders and they would just prefer to refund me my money instead. Additional requests were NOT made for a complimentary necklace, further specific components, and inventory reservations beyond the specific items that are shown in the attachment that were agreed upon! So, I was even more disappointed and dissatisfied by the experience and lack of customer service and their promise of delivering a service and product that they did not fulfill and care to deliver! Also, their disappointing complimentary choice of beverage was tap or sparkling water (pink lemonade or apple juice were never mentioned or offered at any time). 😡👎 #racoduo

We stayed 2 nights for our anniversary. We had heard good things and we wanted to love this place, but we were very disappointed.

The picture shows a nice big couch for lounging but when we got there, in its place were 2 uncomfortable chairs. The picture shows 2 robes waiting on the bed - we had no robes; only 4 small towels were provided which were soaked the 1st night after using them for the hot tub and shower and there was nowhere to hang them to dry.
Since we wanted to cook we brought our own food, but the fridge was missing pieces so it didn’t fit. We also couldn’t eat our oatmeal because there were no bowls in the kitchen.
There were only 4 coffee pods for 2 people for 2 days which cost $2 extra, which is ridiculous after what we paid.
There was no outside light when we wanted to bbq around 8:30 pm. We found a lantern with the handle broken off and rust all along the bottom that did not turn on. We had to use the flashlights on our cell phones for light.
The curtains in the bedroom were broken, the curtain holder downstairs also broken and missing. There was a full sized wine fridge but no decanter.

We paid over $1200 for 2 nights of what we thought would be luxury, and we were sadly mistaken. Would not recommend this place and would not come back.

Drivers are negligent and company business practices are dishonest.

One of their drivers was delivering to the construction site next door and demolished our address sign. Didn’t bother to own up to it, of course. After several phone calls, someone came out and managed to get it to stand upright but it isn’t secure. He claimed it was temporary and someone else would come out and fix it properly on Monday; this happened on Saturday. That would have been fine if it had actually been true. Someone snuck by on Sunday and painted the new wood on the crappy sign white. I told the person on the phone, as well as the guy who “temporarily” fixed the sign that it couldn’t be repaired and would have to be rebuilt and set back into the ground, and that the lights would have to be replaced. The original sign was secured into the ground with concrete. One side was snapped off at ground level and the other is now loose. On the broken off side, the new piece is resting on the ground with a jenky brace piece across and the other side is still loose, the little solar lights on top that illuminated the sign at night are all broken and the custom ordered sign with the numbers (similar to a street sign) is bent. They also left debris all over the ground. While the people I spoke with on the phone, and the guy who came out to “temporarily” put the sign back up were all nice enough, all indications are that they never intended to do any more than bare minimum all along, and only because we caught them and contacted the dispatch office.

Very disappointing experience with my hair smoothening treatment. I had already told them about my previous smoothening treatment from two years ago, but my hair became extremely dry, dull, damaged, and started breaking badly. My waist-length hair had to be cut by around 5–6 inches and is now shoulder-length.

The treatment was very painful, my roots were pulled roughly, and I experienced significant hair fall. They told me they were using L’Oréal products but did not show me the product or expiry date beforehand. At the end, they applied Botox cream to my already damaged hair, which caused severe tangling. Removing the tangles was extremely painful and caused more breakage.
Even after all this, they only told me to use a hair mask.
Overall, I am extremely dissatisfied with the service, the way my hair was handled, and the damage caused. Very unprofessional experience.

(Hi
Thank you for your response.
I understand that hair history can affect the outcome, and I did explain my previous chemical treatments and hair condition before the service.

However, my concern is not simply about the result. I was very disappointed with the condition of my hair afterward, as well as the way my hair was handled by the staff. My biggest concern was actually the staff’s behaviour and the way my hair was treated during the service. I felt that my hair was handled very roughly, and the overall experience was extremely uncomfortable and upsetting.

The next day, I also noticed what appeared to be blood on my scalp, which was very concerning to me.

When I raised concerns that my hair was damaged, the Botox cream was applied without properly dividing my hair into sections. My hair became severely tangled, and while trying to remove the tangles, my hair was handled very roughly. This made the experience even more painful and concerning and, in my opinion, contributed to further damage.

I appreciate that you say you would never knowingly use expired products. However, from a customer’s perspective, I believe it is reasonable to ask to see the product details before a chemical treatment is performed, especially when the hair has already undergone previous treatments.)

Came in for an alignment and left with a clicking steering wheel. When I returned, the staff were rude and dismissive, though they eventually refunded the alignment. An independent mechanic later found a torn rack and pinion boot, caused by twisting the tie rod without releasing the boot during their service. I now have to pay out-of-pocket for replacement parts and repair labor.

Let’s address the owner’s response with a few simple questions:
•​Was there any clicking noise BEFORE your shop performed the alignment?
•​Does replacing struts or shocks require twisting the tie rods inside the rack boots? (No, but adjusting alignment directly involves rotating tie rods).
•​Did your staff not yell at me and hang up the phone during our call?
•​Did you not dismiss work done by another licensed shop as just a "garage repair"?
•​Did you not hand me a cash refund only after the dispute reached a breaking point?

​Everything on my vehicle worked fine until this alignment.

To any prospective customers reading the shop's response: I strongly advise taking your business elsewhere.

one_star_reviews.text:
For reference, expect to pay over $1,000 plus GST to rent a room in this space, only to face significant operational disruptions and what I experienced as a failure by the sublandlords to uphold sublease terms. If you are a regulated clinician looking to rent here, be aware of the following issues I encountered during my time at We Wellness Space:

• Extreme Temperature Inconsistencies: The boiler was turned on or the AC stopped working unpredictably without proper communication. This resulted in my office hitting 30 degrees for days at a time, severely affecting clients (especially those on medications impacting temperature regulation). This directly disrupted my client flow and reduced my business revenue.
• Exhaustive Self-Advocacy Required: I had to fight unnecessarily hard to get basic operational needs met by the sublandlords. I quickly found that bypassing them to deal with primary building management was the only way to resolve issues quickly and without hassle (such as obtaining a basic fan for airflow when the office became a health hazard).
• Unreliable Infrastructure: The internet failed roughly 25% of the time, forcing me to rely on my own phone hotspot and rendering the shared printer/scanner unusable when needed most. Amenities and client refreshments were frequently entirely unstocked.
• Pest Issues: Experienced recurring issues with flies, wasps, and Asian ladybugs inside the private office.
• Severe Noise & Confidentiality Concerns: There is a severe lack of soundproofing between units. I could clearly hear neighbouring subtenants, as well as people vacuuming and socializing right outside my door while I was in session. This creates major concerns for practitioners managing strict patient confidentiality and privacy protocols.
• Unprofessional Waiting Room Boundaries: I witnessed a distinct lack of clinical professionalism in the common waiting area. In one instance, a sublandlord encountered a client they knew and chose to openly acknowledge them and remain in the waiting room socializing with others in front of that client. This demonstrated a severe lack of clinical boundaries, causing visible discomfort and compromising what should be a safe, discreet space for people awaiting therapy or care.
• Diluted Clinical Identity: Despite being marketed toward mental health and clinical professionals, tenant vetting is purely transactional. The space allows completely unregulated practices (such as astrology and reiki masters) to operate out of the unit, creating professional friction for those bound by PHIA.
• Avoidant Management & Accommodation Failures: Management proved highly conflict-avoidant and unwilling to engage in collaborative problem-solving, which was particularly disappointing given that a sublandlord is a practicing therapist. Furthermore, as a practitioner with a disability, I found their handling of accommodation requests to be deeply unprofessional and personally weaponized rather than structurally supported.

Proceed with extreme caution if you rely on a stable, professional, and confidential space to run a regulated healthcare practice. The sublandlords are inexperienced when it comes to private practice and running a business, and their primary focus is generating passive income.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing experience with Medcentre Health in Scarborough.

I don’t have an Ontario health card, so I understand that I have to pay out of pocket. But the way this clinic handled my situation felt like they cared far more about collecting another fee than actually following up on a patient.

On my first visit for a blocked/muffled ear, I was charged $120. The doctor saw me for roughly 2 minutes, checked my ear and prescribed ear drops. My condition did not improve.

I returned and was charged another $90 just to see a doctor again. I was then told I needed an ear wash, which cost another $30. After the procedure, I was told the wax was removed and that my hearing should improve within a few hours.

It has now been approximately 48 hours, and my ear is still blocked with no noticeable improvement.

What frustrated me the most was the follow-up. I called the clinic because the treatment they provided had not resolved the issue, and instead of offering any meaningful follow-up or even discussing the situation, I was essentially told that I would need to pay again to see them or go somewhere else.

So after spending $240 in total for the same unresolved ear problem, their response was basically to pay them again.

I understand that private medical services cost money, but patients should also expect a reasonable standard of care and follow-up, especially after multiple paid visits and a procedure.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend this clinic to anyone paying out of pocket. Ask clearly about every fee and their follow-up policy before receiving treatment.

I didn’t have a great experience picking up my package at this location. It was my graduation photo package, and Canada Post was originally supposed to deliver it to my house, but instead it was redirected to this pharmacy for pickup.

When I went there with my mom, the lady dealing with us was extremely rude and disrespectful. My mom was on the phone talking to her friend, and she wasn’t even being loud or disturbing anyone. The lady rudely told her to get off the phone and then told my mom to get out of the store. There was absolutely no reason to speak to her like that.

The whole interaction was very uncomfortable, and I felt that the way my mom was treated was discriminatory and racist. Whether someone is picking up a Canada Post package or shopping at the pharmacy, customers should be treated with basic respect.

Canada Post should seriously look into how customers are being treated at authorized pickup locations. I expected much better, especially since I didn’t even choose to have my package sent here in the first place. I really hope Canada Post does not redirect any of my future packages to this location.

Very disappointing experience and extremely disrespectful customer service.

I am writing to raise a concern regarding my recent order from the Ajax location. I ordered an Extra Large \(14\-inch\) pizza, but unfortunately, the overall experience was very disappointing.

First, I did not feel that the pizza was actually worthy of being considered Extra Large, especially considering the price. More importantly, more than half of the pizza appeared to have little to no seasoning. As you can see in the attached picture, almost 3 inches around the edges was essentially just plain bread, with no sauce, toppings, or seasoning.

I have been a long-time fan of Karachi Pizza, and my family and I have been ordering from you almost every weekend for the past year. That is why this experience was particularly disappointing and unexpected.

When I spoke with the customer representative at the store, I was told that there are some corporate cost-cutting measures currently taking place. I understand that businesses have to manage their costs, but this should not come at the expense of the quality of a product that customers are paying full price for. A customer should still receive a properly prepared pizza with an appropriate amount of sauce, toppings, and seasoning.

I truly enjoy Karachi Pizza and would prefer to continue ordering from you, but the quality and service seem to have been declining recently. This particular experience, however, was not acceptable.

I kindly request that you look into this matter and provide an appropriate resolution. I hope this feedback is taken seriously and that the quality standards at the Ajax location can be improved.

I’m very disappointed with my experience at this clinic.

Before booking my appointment, I called the receptionist to ask about tummy liposuction. She told me that I needed to book an appointment for an evaluation. I specifically asked how much the procedure would cost because I wanted to know the approximate price before coming to the clinic. She told me it would be around $3,000–$4,000, which was reasonableto booked consultation, so I decided to booked.

I also asked about the consultation fee, and I was told it would be $200 + taxes. I paid $229.95 for the appointment.

When I arrived and saw the doctor, he was told that I needed a tummy tuck with liposuction, and that the cost would be approximately $18,900 before tax, including the evaluation. I was also told that liposuction alone was not an option for me.

My main concern is that the receptionist gave me a price range of $3,000–$4,000 when I called, but that price was not applicable to the procedure the doctor said I needed. If had been told from the beginning that the receptionist did not know the price or that the doctor might recommend a tummy tuck with liposuction  3 zone costing around $18,900 before tax, I would not have booked the appointment.

I spent $229.95 for a consultation that ultimately did not meet what I was expecting based on the information I received over the phone.

I believe patients should be given clear and accurate information about pricing before paying for a consultation, especially when the difference is thousands of dollars. I hope the clinic improves its communication with patients so that others do not have the same experience.

The food itself was even worse. The chicken was extremely disappointing — I could barely tell what I was eating, and it did not seem properly cooked to me. I found the meal disgusting and completely inedible, and I ended up regretting buying it.

What bothered me most was the way my concerns were handled. Instead of acknowledging why I was questioning the incorrect items on the receipt, the staff acted as though there was no problem and smiled it off. That left me feeling misled and taken advantage of as a customer.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend Pride and Spice. Customers deserve accurate receipts, properly prepared food, and straightforward answers when they raise a concern. I certainly did not feel that I received any of those things here.

one_star_reviews.text:
I’m extremely disappointed with the way I was treated at the JD Sports in Masonville.

I was purchasing Nike shoes that were more than $200. I specifically asked for a brand-new pair because the display pair had clearly been tried on multiple times. The employee told me he would get me a new pair, but instead, he put the other display shoe into a size 7 box and tried to give it to us as if it were new. We only caught this because the cashier noticed it was actually a size 7.5 a size 7 shoe in a size 7 box.

What makes this worse is that I had already made it very clear that I did NOT want a display pair. If there was no new pair available, he could have simply been honest instead of trying to pass off a display shoe as new.

When we pointed this out, instead of apologizing or handling the situation professionally, he became extremely loud and argumentative. He was even holding the shoes very close to my mom’s face while insisting they were “fully brand new.” It was completely unnecessary and made an already frustrating situation much worse.

We still purchased the shoes because we liked them, but honestly, spending more than $200 should not come with having to question whether an employee is being truthful about what we’re buying.

The issue wasn’t just the shoes it was the dishonesty and the disrespectful way the situation was handled, seeing the 1 star reviews talking about customer service is honestly so true.

We buzzed for help at the exit machine and noone answered. We then found security who were to unhelpful. All we wanted to do was pay the fee to leave. The security guards kept telling us the ticket we had was not the original ticket, which we initially mentioned to them. We wasted half an hour just trying to get out of the parking garage. All we wanted to do was pay the fee and leave. Security finally helped us pay at the exit and apologized to us. What's the point of apologizing when it was very simple to fix. We also called the customer service line of Precise Parking and the person on the phone was so rude. She kept telling us to press the buzzer and someone would come help us. We kept mentioning that we have tired that. Overall, the parking garage itself is great. But the lack of problem-solving amongst the security guard's is ridiculous. I don't know why it took three security guard's just to tell us how to pay one fixed fee. To be honest, I would probably never park there again just because of how terrible security is. It's a parking garage and there are going to be problems regarding tickets sometimes. If you can't solve the problems, then that in itself is an issue. They just ruined our entire night with their lack of urgency and care.

My experience with Pollin was extremely disappointing and, honestly, felt like a complete waste of my time and money.

The care team gave me the impression that they were not sure what they were doing. I spent considerable time and money going through different approaches, but unfortunately, I saw no meaningful results. It often felt like I was being used for trial and error rather than receiving a clear, well-planned, and personalized approach to my care.

What made the experience even worse was the lack of empathy and poor communication. When you are already investing your time, money, and trust into a service, you expect the people caring for you to listen, communicate clearly, and genuinely understand your concerns. I did not feel that way here.

As an African, I was particularly uncomfortable with how the process felt at times. I felt like my concerns were not being properly understood and that I was being treated more like an experiment than a person whose time and money mattered.

After everything I invested, having nothing meaningful to show for it was incredibly frustrating.

I would strongly encourage anyone considering Pollin to do their research and think carefully before committing their time and money. Based on my experience, I would not recommend it.
